texts.preamble: Mahavir Jain vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 March, 2026 Author: Ramesh Sinha Bench: Ramesh Sinha 1 2026:C High Court Of Chhattisgarh At Bilaspur Mcrc No. 1901 of 2026 Mahavir Jain S/o. Lalit Kumar Jain, Aged About 35 Years R/o. Pan Kali Mai, Ward No. 14, Mungeli, Police Station, Tehsil And Distr (C.G.) versus State of Chhattisgarh Through Police Station City Kotwali, Munge Mungeli C.G. For Applicant : Mr. Manoj Paranjape, Senior Adv Digitally signed by Verma, Advocate. Abhishek Abhishek Shrivas Shrivas Date: 2026.03.13 For Non-applicant/State. : Mr. S.S. Baghel, Govt. Advocate 11:35:07 +0530 Hon'ble Mr. Ramesh Sinha, Chief Justice Order on Board 12.03.2026 1.
texts.facts: As per the case of the prosecution, a ticket/alert was received in the Satark App of ICCC, Raipur on 10.01.2026 regarding fake paddy lifting/transportation/delivery and possible fabricated transportation activities in connivance with certain paddy procurement centres. The data relating to overloading of vehicles beyond their registered carrying capacity was analyzed, in which it was found that some vehicles were carrying loads exceeding more than 200% of their registered carrying capacity, which was technically not possible. In reference to the said alert/ticket, an investigation team was constituted by the office of the Collector, District Mungeli, Chhattisgarh, vide Order No. 1971/E/Steno Additional Collector/2026 Mungeli dated 12.01.2026. During the ongoing paddy procurement work at 105 procurement centres in the district under the government support price scheme, the data relating to overloading of vehicles was analyzed at the state level by ICCC, Raipur. During such analysis, it came to the notice of the authorities that some vehicles were carrying loads ranging from more than 200% up to 1,117% of their registered vehicle capacity. 3. In this regard, the investigation team constituted for inspection of the concerned paddy procurement centres and rice mills, in accordance with the rules, inspected the mill-cum-warehouse premises of Vardhman Rice Mill (MM-402727) and Vardhman Milling Industries (MM-40352) located at Pandariya Road, Mungeli, on 12.01.2026 and 13.01.2026. At the time of inspection, 556 bags of paddy were found in excess in the mill-cum- warehouse premises, and no evidence or document was produced to justify the excess stock. Further, 494 plastic bags were found stored in the mill. The rice mill operator did not produce any register or document related to the mill, nor any data backup from the date of paddy lifting till the date of inspection. Additionally, 4,900 bags (2,450 quintals) were found stored in plain plastic bags in Vardhman Rice Mill (MM-402727) and Vardhman Milling Industries (MM-40352), which prima facie appeared to be rice meant for distribution to ration card holders under the Public Distribution System (PDS). As per law, samples were sent to the Food Safety Officer, District Mungeli, for examination by the office of the Collector (Food Branch), District Mungeli. It is further alleged that low- capacity vehicles operated by Mahavir Jain S/o Lalit Kumar Jain, operator of Vardhman Rice Mill (MM-402727), made 42 trips, for which false gate passes were issued for transportation exceeding 5,689 quintals of paddy, beyond the carrying capacity of the vehicles. It is alleged that by issuing false Delivery Memos (DM) by the concerned procurement centre in-charges, and by colluding in a planned manner, fake transportation was shown, resulting in diversion of the said quantity of paddy, whose estimated value is Rs. 1,76,35,900/-, thereby causing financial loss to the government. 4. Similarly, it is alleged that Mahavir Jain S/o Lalit Kumar Jain, operator of Vardhman Milling Industries (MM-40352), made 30 trips, for which false gate passes were issued for transportation exceeding 4,569 quintals of paddy. By issuing false Delivery Memos (DM) and allegedly colluding with other accused persons in a planned manner, the said quantity of paddy, whose estimated value is Rs. 1,41,63,900/-, was diverted, thereby causing financial loss to the government. Thereafter, the Assistant Food Officer, District Mungeli, submitted a report alleging that the rice mill operators and Mahavir Jain vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140118137/ 2 procurement centre in-charges, in collusion, conspired in an organized and planned manner and deliberately hatched a criminal conspiracy to cause financial loss to the government through deception. On the basis of the said report, a case was registered at Police Station Mungeli against the accused Lalit Kumar Jain S/o Budhmal Jain (Proprietor) and Mahavir Jain S/o Lalit Kumar Jain (Director) and other accused persons. Accordingly, FIR No. 34/2026 dated 20.01.2026 was registered under Sections 318(4) and 316(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and Sections 3 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. During this long period, the applicant's father has always completed his agreements/work with utmost satisfaction, and not a single complaint has ever been made against him. It is further submitted that the applicant is not involved in any manner whatsoever in the functioning of Vardhman Rice Mill (MM 402727) and Vardhman Milling Industries (MM 40352), having their registered office at Nawagaon, Pandaria Road, Mungeli (C.G.). Both the firms are registered in the name of Lalit Kumar Jain, who is the sole proprietor of the said firms. The said firms are also registered under the GST Act, bearing Registration Nos. 22ACIPJ2717M1ZN and 22ACIPJ2721M2ZM, respectively. On 24.11.2025, an agreement was executed between Lalit Kumar Jain, Proprietor of Vardhman Rice Mill (MM 402727), and the DMO, Mungeli, for lifting paddy for Lot Nos. 4646 to 4810 and Lot Nos. 4811 to 4980, vide Agreement Nos. AC11205630029 and AC112025630030, respectively. On 26.11.2025, another agreement was executed between Lalit Kumar Jain, Proprietor of Vardhman Milling Industries (MM 40352), and the DMO, Mungeli, for lifting paddy for Lot Nos. 6776 to 6950 and Lot Nos. 6951 to 7115, vide Agreement Nos. AC11205630051 and AC112025630052, respectively. From the bare perusal of the agreement executed between Lalit Kumar Jain (Proprietor of Vardhman Rice Mill MM 402727) and DMO, Mungeli, it is evident that the agreement was executed on 24.11.2025 and remained valid up to 23.05.2026. During the said period, the firm of the applicant's father was required to lift approximately 62,880.00 quintals of paddy for the purpose of custom milling (Arva). It is also submitted that from the bare perusal of the agreement executed between Lalit Kumar Jain (Proprietor of Vardhman Milling Industries MM 40352) and DMO, Mungeli, it is evident that the agreement was executed on 26.11.2025 and remained valid up to 25.05.2026. The quantity of paddy so lifted was present in the mill of the applicant's father, which has also been mentioned in the inspection report prepared by the inspection committee during the time of inspection. In fact, 222.40 quintals of paddy were found in excess, which were also seized from the mill. As per the agreements bearing Nos. AC11205630029, AC112025630030, AC11205630051, and Mahavir Jain vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140118137/ 3 AC112025630052, the paddy was lifted from the procurement centers and DO & DM were issued in favour of the mill of the applicant's father. All such DOs are entered online on the Government portal, and the entries are regularly updated and monitored by Government authorities. It is further submitted that only authorized Government officials are permitted to make entries on the said portal. The applicant's father, being the sole proprietor of the mill, can only access the information, and the same cannot be modified or forged by the applicant in any manner. It has been alleged that 222.40 quintals of paddy were found in excess in the mill of the applicant's father. It is pertinent to mention that the applicant, Mahavir Jain, is the registered owner of the following agricultural lands: 1. Land bearing Khasra Nos. 81/5, 81/6, 81/7, 81/9, admeasuring 2.3 hectares, situated at Village Baiharsari. 2. Land bearing Khasra Nos. 97/2, 99/1, 99/2, 99/3, 99/4, 100/1, admeasuring 2.04 hectares, situated at Village Madanpur. 3. Land bearing Khasra No. 254/3, admeasuring 0.21 hectare, situated at Village Mohtara. All the aforesaid lands are agricultural lands and are duly recorded in the revenue records in the name of the applicant Mahavir Jain. The said lands are being used by the applicant and his father Lalit Kumar Jain for cultivation purposes, and they regularly cultivate the same and produce paddy from the said lands. It is submitted that the paddy which was allegedly found in excess, i.e., 222.40 quintals, is self- cultivated produce from the agricultural lands of the applicant Mahavir Jain. The same was stored in the warehouse of the mill for safety purposes, in order to protect it from environmental degradation, biological pests, and to maintain the quality of the produce. As per the contents of the F.I.R. itself, the samples of rice seized from the mill of the applicant's father were sent to the Food Safety Officer, District Mungeli, for examination by the Office of the Collector (Food Branch), District Mungeli, on 19.01.2026. Thereafter, an analysis report dated 20.01.2026 was prepared by the Food Analyst, State Food Testing Laboratory, Food and Drug Administration, Raipur. From the bare perusal of the said report, it is evident that the rice was free from insects, larvae, and fungus growth, and that the custom milling was carried out in accordance with the standards prescribed under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. This clearly indicates that the custom milling work at the applicant's father's mill was being carried out properly and in compliance with Government norms, and that the rice sent for analysis was freshly milled rice from the current procurement. In fact, no loss has been caused to the paddy procurement centre, and there is no wrongful gain or wrongful loss, which is one of the essential ingredients of the offence of cheating. The Joint Secretary, Government of Chhattisgarh, Food Civil Supplies and Consumer Protection Department, issued a Circular dated 15.10.2025 regarding procurement of paddy at the support price for the Kharif Marketing Year 2025-26.
texts.arguments: 5. Mr. Paranjape, learned Senior Advocate submits that the present applicant is innocent person and has been falsely been implicated in the foresaid case. It is submitted the age of the applicant is 35 years, and if he is kept behind bars, it would cause severe mental as well as physical agony to the applicant. The applicant's father has been engaged in the business of custom milling for many years and has been operating the mill since the year 1993-94, i.e., for the past more than 32 years. 6. Mr. Paranjape further submits that as per the terms and conditions of the agreements executed between the parties, the paddy was lifted from the paddy procurement centers, Mungeli. As per Clause 16.5 of the said circular, the following direction has been issued regarding transportation of paddy: "To lift paddy from procurement centres and to avoid double transportation costs, the maximum quantity of paddy should be supplied directly to the millers.". It is submitted that the present applicant has no criminal antecedents and he is in jail since 20.01.2026, conclusion of the trial may take some time, therefore, he prays for grant of regular bail. 7. On the other hand, learned State counsel opposes the bail application of the present applicant and submits that the charge-sheet has already been submitted before the competent Court in the present case.
